text.arabic_uthmani: فَمَنِ ٱبْتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ

words.gloss_range: resumptive and consequential connector that opens the converse conditional branch from the prior permission
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the ayah begin as a consequence of the prior boundary, not as an isolated maxim. It resumes from 70:30 and opens the converse case: once the exception has been stated, whoever moves outside it must be judged. The first particle also anticipates the second {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) at word 6, so the verse is heard as a double-hinged frame: condition first, verdict second.

topics.headline: conditional branch from prior permission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the condemnation grows directly out of the preceding exception in 70:30 rather than starting a new detached rule.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a resumptive/consequential conjunction, and the attachment evidence links the following words as the conditional protasis.

topics.headline: first half of the double connector frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verse's logic being bracketed by two matching connectors, with the first opening the condition and the second delivering the verdict.
topics.reason: The same particle appears at word 1 and word 6, and the clause evidence assigns word 6 to the apodosis.

topics.headline: bound connector fuses with the condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that consequence and conditional actor arrive as one compact onset rather than as a slow restart.
topics.reason: The one-letter particle is attached to the following conditional pronoun in the surface opening.

words.gloss_range: conditional and relative whoever-pronoun that supplies the seeker as subject and universalizes the ruling

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the verb whose action is performed by the conditional subject

words.prose: {{ar:مَنِ}} ({{tr:mani}}) turns the next act into an open legal condition: whoever seeks beyond the boundary falls under the verdict. It is the subject of {{ar:ٱبْتَغَىٰ}} ({{tr:ibtaghā}}), not the thing sought, so responsibility stays on the seeker. The same small indeclinable form can work conditionally and relatively, opening the rule while preparing the later class-identification reading. Although the form is singular, the apodosis resumes it with plural demonstrative and pronoun forms, converting any individual case into a classified group; its light nasal onset also makes the move into the heavier action verb audible.

topics.headline: whoever opens general conditional scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rule applies to any person who satisfies the condition, not to a named offender.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as a conditional or relative pronoun, and the attachment evidence makes it the head of the protasis.

topics.headline: singular agent becomes plural verdict class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammar moving from one possible seeker to the plural class identified in the verdict.
topics.reason: The local attachment makes this pronoun the subject of the verb, while the apodosis resumes the condition with plural demonstrative and pronoun forms.

topics.headline: compact form carries conditional and relative force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one small indeclinable form can both open the rule and support the later class-identification reading.
topics.reason: The same visible form bears the conditional and relative readings, and its cliticized opening compresses the connector and condition.

topics.headline: light nasal onset leads into the act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an audible shift from the light conditional onset into the heavier action verb.
topics.reason: The sound row gives a local recitation payoff that supports, but does not change, the syntactic conditional reading.

words.gloss_range: self-directed seeking in a completed conditional frame, with the sought object left unnamed and the boundary-space complement doing the local work
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes seeking, desire, wrongful overreach, excess, and propriety contrasts; local grammar selects seeking while the boundary phrase keeps transgressive pressure active

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the beyond-that boundary phrase that fills the local complement space
the final transgressor predicate answering the seeking act

words.prose: {{ar:ٱبْتَغَىٰ}} ({{tr:ibtaghā}}) is the action-core of the protasis. Its perfect Form VIII shape treats the pursuit as a completed, self-involved act for judgment, while the missing direct object keeps the specific object unnamed and lets {{ar:وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:warāʾa dhālika}}) supply the decisive boundary-space. The local sense is seeking, but the {{ar:ب غ ي}} ({{tr:b-gh-y}}) field of desire, excess, and wrongful overreach makes the seeking already lean toward the final label {{ar:ٱلْعَادُونَ}} ({{tr:al-ʿādūna}}). The same seeking-beyond wording recurs in the paired boundary formula (23:7), so this is a repeated legal mechanism, not a one-off spatial phrase. Even the cadence carries the act toward the verdict, with long open vowels stretching through the boundary phrase and the back-throat sound of the verb answered by the final pharyngeal onset.

topics.headline: perfect verb triggers the condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse treats the pursuit as the completed act that activates the legal verdict.
topics.reason: The verb is a perfect Form VIII verb governed by the conditional pronoun, and the attachment evidence makes it the head of the protasis.

topics.headline: object-space is beyond the boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the offense is framed as pursuit toward a boundary-space, not as taking a separately named object.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence marks only the accusative adverbial complement, and the translation support warns against supplying a direct object beyond that frame.

topics.headline: seeking carries wrongful-overreach pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the selected sense is seeking, but in this boundary frame the seeking is already morally charged as overreach.
topics.reason: The local verb still means seeking, but the boundary complement licenses the CRITICAL pressure from desire and excess toward transgression without replacing the selected sense.

topics.headline: Form VIII keeps pursuit self-directed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the morphology keeps responsibility on the actor's own pursuit, while stronger claims about ego or craving remain interpretive pressure rather than the lexical sense itself.
topics.reason: QAC gives Form VIII active perfect, so self-directed pursuit survives; the stronger self-interest language is kept as narrowed payoff rather than a separate gloss.

topics.headline: seeking beyond repeats as legal formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the seeking-beyond phrase is the same boundary formula found in 23:7.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the concrete parallel at 23:7, and the local wording matches the same act-boundary-verdict configuration.

topics.headline: act leans forward to verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that sound, root pressure, and closure all make the opening act answerable by the final transgressor label.
topics.reason: The sound rows and summary row preserve a real local payoff, while the root relation is already constrained by the selected seeking sense.

words.gloss_range: accusative place-adverb meaning beyond or behind, locally selected as the boundary-space toward which the seeking is directed
words.root_gloss_range: root and lexical range includes beyond, behind, after, outside, and concealment-related imagery; the local adverbial construction selects boundary-beyond while leaving hidden other-side pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the demonstrative landmark governed by the boundary adverb

words.prose: {{ar:وَرَآءَ}} ({{tr:warāʾa}}) is where the seeking is aimed. As an accusative place-adverb governing {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}), it turns the prior permission into a measured line with an outside, so the condition becomes spatial: seeking beyond that. Its wider beyond/behind and concealment range is narrowed locally to boundary-beyond, while still making the prohibited side feel like the other, screened side of the limit. The word stays directional rather than becoming a concealment verb, and its medial hamza creates a small catch at the very boundary term. The same threshold phrase recurs in the paired formula (23:7), anchoring the legal topology of permitted inside and transgressive beyond.

topics.headline: adverbial boundary-space for the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the act is directed into a space beyond the limit rather than toward an ordinary named object.
topics.reason: The word is parsed as an accusative place adverb attached to the verb, and attachment evidence treats it as the local complement span.

topics.headline: governs the that-landmark
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demonstrative is not vague; it is grammatically bound as the landmark from which beyond is measured.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following demonstrative as the genitive complement of the construct-like adverb.

topics.headline: beyond selected, behind and hidden pressure retained
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local meaning is beyond the rule, while the wider behind and hidden-side range gives that beyond a concrete other-side feel.
topics.reason: The legal boundary phrase selects spatial beyond; other root-range and lexical pressures survive as image rather than as alternate local senses.

topics.headline: adverbial form and hamza catch mark the boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the word as a directional adverb with a small audible catch at the boundary term itself.
topics.reason: The local form is an adverbial, not a finite concealment verb; the sound rows add a recitation-level payoff without changing the grammar.

topics.headline: threshold phrase repeats in 23:7
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this beyond-that threshold is a repeated legal phrase also found in 23:7.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply the concrete 23:7 parallel, and the local phrase matches the same boundary formula.

words.gloss_range: distal singular demonstrative that gathers the prior exception into one governed boundary landmark
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) is the landmark after {{ar:وَرَآءَ}} ({{tr:warāʾa}}), not a new subject. It points back across the ayah boundary to the exception in 70:30 and compresses that multi-part permission into one singular referent. Placed at the end of the protasis, it becomes the threshold word: the condition closes on that boundary, then the verdict begins. The same pointer is part of the repeated beyond-that boundary formula (23:7), where prior permission is likewise made into a threshold.

topics.headline: that points back to 70:30
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word forces 70:30 into view, because the current boundary cannot be resolved without the prior exception.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence says the demonstrative points back to the immediately preceding exception domain and recommends the 70:30 reading window.

topics.headline: genitive landmark after beyond
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demonstrative supplies the fixed point from which crossing is measured, rather than adding fresh content.
topics.reason: The local parse makes the demonstrative the genitive complement of the boundary adverb.

topics.headline: singular pointer compresses plural legal content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a complex permission is treated as one bounded legal unit that can be crossed.
topics.reason: The singular masculine demonstrative summarizes a conceptually multi-part prior exception without enumerating it again.

topics.headline: threshold before the verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the condition ending on the boundary-marker before the apodosis begins.
topics.reason: The word closes the protasis at the point where the second connector introduces the apodosis.

topics.headline: pointer belongs to the repeated formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demonstrative is part of the repeated beyond-that boundary formula also seen in 23:7.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL row gives the 23:7 formula, and the same demonstrative completes the threshold phrase in 70:31.

words.gloss_range: apodosis connector that turns the following nominal clause into the required consequence of the condition

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the demonstrative subject bound to the apodosis connector

words.prose: The second {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the verdict hinge. It is not another opening resumption; it answers the conditional protasis and binds the following nominal identification to it as consequence. It also closes the double-{{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) frame begun at the ayah's first word: branch from the prior rule, then deliver the classification. Because it is attached to {{ar:أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulāʾika}}), the ruling begins without a gap: condition, then those people, then the restrictive identity.

topics.headline: second connector marks the answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the nominal clause is the required answer to the condition, not an independent comment.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the following clause as the apodosis introduced by this connector.

topics.headline: double connector closes the frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first connector opening the condition and this second connector closing it with judgment.
topics.reason: The two particles occupy the structural turns of the ayah: branch and verdict.

topics.headline: attached particle launches the demonstrative verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a brief reset before the verdict, with the consequence fused directly to the demonstrative subject.
topics.reason: The particle is written and heard with the following demonstrative, and the sound rows preserve the local two-beat condition-verdict effect.

topics.headline: apodosis prepares restricted classification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this connector and the later separating pronoun together make the verdict tightly bound and restrictive.
topics.reason: The connector introduces the nominal apodosis, while the predicate structure is strengthened by the later separator.

words.gloss_range: distal plural demonstrative that resumes the conditional actor as a classified group and begins the nominal verdict clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the separating pronoun in the verdict chain
the final predicate naming the transgressor class

words.prose: {{ar:أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulāʾika}}) starts the verdict by pointing to the people produced by the condition. Its distal plural form turns the singular whoever of the protasis into a visible class, held at classificatory distance before the predicate names it. The long marked deictic contour slows the verdict onset before {{ar:هُمُ}} ({{tr:humu}}) and {{ar:ٱلْعَادُونَ}} ({{tr:al-ʿādūna}}) lock the identity. The demonstrative also controls that plural agreement chain, so the ruling attaches to the actors, not to the abstract act alone; it begins the condemned side of the boundary classification after the protected side in 70:30.

topics.headline: distal demonstrative classifies the actors
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the apodosis identifies the offenders as a pointed, distanced class rather than addressing them directly.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a plural demonstrative, and attachment evidence says it resumes the conditional group.

topics.headline: singular condition becomes plural class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that any one seeker is gathered into a plural category under the verdict.
topics.reason: The demonstrative points back to the conditional pronoun while appearing in plural form at the start of the nominal clause.

topics.headline: plural demonstrative controls the verdict chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the demonstrative, separator, and definite predicate forming a restrictive identification rather than a loose description.
topics.reason: The local predication evidence places the final predicate after the demonstrative chain, with the intervening pronoun as separator.

topics.headline: long demonstrative marks the verdict onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verdict beat slowing on a marked deictic form before the final identity is spoken.
topics.reason: The recitation-oriented rows give a local payoff for the marked surface shape at the beginning of the apodosis.

topics.headline: current condemned group mirrors prior protected group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the apodosis beginning the opposite side of the prior boundary classification: protected inside, condemned beyond.
topics.reason: The boundary row links the pronoun-chain mirror across 70:30 and 70:31, and the local order starts the verdict with the demonstrative subject.

words.gloss_range: independent third-person plural pronoun functioning as separator and resumptive pronoun in the nominal verdict

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the demonstrative subject before the separating pronoun
the definite predicate after the separating pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:هُمُ}} ({{tr:humu}}) is the small word that locks the verdict into identity. Read as a separating pronoun, it prevents {{ar:ٱلْعَادُونَ}} ({{tr:al-ʿādūna}}) from collapsing into an adjective after {{ar:أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ}} ({{tr:ulāʾika}}); read referentially, it explicitly resumes the group now being classified. Its retention adds a pronominal beat before the final predicate, making the clause restrictive: those are the transgressors. The short nasal-labial sound works as an audible hinge between the longer demonstrative and the final label, and the repeated pronoun machinery mirrors the opposite legal identity stated in 70:30.

topics.headline: separator turns description into equation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause identifies the group as the transgressors rather than merely describing them as transgressing.
topics.reason: The pronoun stands between demonstrative subject and definite predicate, matching the separating-pronoun function described in the CRITICAL rows.

topics.headline: pronoun creates restrictive identification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verdict as a restricted identification of this class, not a weaker attributive phrase.
topics.reason: The final predicate is definite and follows the intervening pronoun, supporting the restrictive-equation reading.

topics.headline: pronoun resumes the pointed group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same group pointed out by the demonstrative is restated before the final label.
topics.reason: The referential reading remains compatible with the separator reading because both point to the same plural group in the apodosis.

topics.headline: retained independent pronoun gives closure weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verdict delayed by a deliberate pronominal beat before the final predicate lands.
topics.reason: The pronoun is overt even though a nominal clause could be formed more lightly, creating a separate beat in the verdict.

topics.headline: pronoun mirrors the prior exoneration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same pronominal machinery helping mark opposite legal identities across 70:30 and 70:31.
topics.reason: The boundary rows connect the prior not-blameworthy identity with the current transgressor identity through repeated pronoun structure.

topics.headline: short pronoun audibly hinges the verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the short nasal-labial beat joining the demonstrative to the final predicate.
topics.reason: The sound row gives a local audible payoff that aligns with the pronoun's syntactic hinge role.

words.gloss_range: definite active participle predicate naming the boundary-crossers as the recognized transgressor class
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes crossing beyond a limit, aggression, hostility, and rushing past; local predicate selects transgression while those physical and adversarial pressures sharpen the verdict

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the seeking act answered by the final transgressor label
the boundary phrase that defines what has been crossed
the separating pronoun before the final predicate

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعَادُونَ}} ({{tr:al-ʿādūna}}) is the verse's verdict seal. The definite active participle, after {{ar:هُمُ}} ({{tr:humu}}), names a recognized human class: not merely people doing a transgressive act, but the transgressors. Its simple Form I participle gives a plain categorical verdict rather than an intensified or reflexive derived form. The selected {{ar:ع د و}} ({{tr:ʿ-d-w}}) sense is boundary-crossing, while the root's rushing and hostile ranges make that crossing feel active and adversarial against the limit marked by {{ar:وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:warāʾa dhālika}}); the secondary return-reading remains only a shadow of repeated relapse, not the governing sense. The exact predicate also closes the same boundary formula in 23:7, and it answers the opening seeking verb by turning the act into identity. Its deep guttural onset and long nasal closure give the final label weight while reversing the prior not-blameworthy status in 70:30.

topics.headline: definite predicate names the known class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause identifies the actors as the transgressor class rather than offering an indefinite description.
topics.reason: QAC marks a definite active participle, and attachment evidence makes it the predicate after the demonstrative-pronoun chain.

topics.headline: active participle makes an agentive human identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word names people characterized by overstepping, not an abstract violation alone.
topics.reason: The masculine plural active participle agrees with the plural demonstrative-pronoun chain and names the acting class.

topics.headline: transgression selected with rushing and hostility pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local label means transgressors, while the root range makes the crossing feel like moving past and against a limit.
topics.reason: The legal boundary context selects transgression; physical rushing and adversarial force survive as lexical pressure rather than alternate predicates.

topics.headline: returning ambiguity remains secondary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a secondary return-to-the-act coloring, while the local and formulaic verdict remains transgressors.
topics.reason: The bundle has root ambiguity in some evidence, but QAC aligns the word with {{ar:ع د و}} ({{tr:ʿ-d-w}}) and the boundary formula selects transgression; return is kept only as narrowed shadow pressure.

topics.headline: plain Form I participle gives categorical verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict is expressed in a simple categorical participle rather than an intensified or reflexive derived form.
topics.reason: The local form is an active participle on the basic pattern, so the derived-form contrasts survive as form-specific payoff.

topics.headline: same verdict closes 23:7 and 70:31
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final predicate is a repeated verdict seal for the same boundary logic in 23:7.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the concrete 23:7 recurrence, and the local predicate occupies the same closing role.

topics.headline: seeking act resolves into transgressor identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving from the condition of seeking beyond to the final identity of transgressors.
topics.reason: The final word closes the nominal apodosis and answers the opening condition with a class label.

topics.headline: sound closure marks the reversal from exoneration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final label landing heavily while reversing the previous verse's not-blameworthy status.
topics.reason: The sound rows and boundary rows give a local payoff for the final landing and the shift from permission to violation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence ابتغى ... وراء ذلك ... العادون joins deliberate pursuit, a far side of a deictic limit, and the resulting identity of boundary-crosser.
baseline_models.mechanism: Desire becomes transgression through directed motion: a person seeks an object, locates it beyond an already indicated perimeter, crosses the exception line, and is consequently classed by that crossing.

activation_trace.role: Seeking and pursuing supplies the initiating, intentional motion toward an object.
The far side, whether behind, ahead, or beyond, gives the pursuit a bounded spatial exterior.
Overstepping a bound into injustice supplies both the completed action and its ethical consequence.
Passing beyond and excepting sharpens the limit as an exception perimeter rather than an unmarked prohibition.

changed_reading.before: A generic warning that some unspecified conduct is excessive.
changed_reading.after: A causal miniature in which purposeful pursuit crosses the exterior of a defined allowance and turns the seeker into a transgressor.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وراء can place the sought object not only past a line but behind visibility, while ابتغى and العادون retain pursuit and overstepping.
baseline_models.mechanism: The exterior can function as concealment: the seeker moves an appetite behind or out of sight of the acknowledged limit, but hiding the pursuit does not remove its boundary-crossing character.

activation_trace.role: Pursuit supplies the deliberate attempt to obtain what is sought.
Covering a thing and putting it out of sight makes the beyond-space a possible zone of evasion.
Boundary violation keeps concealed pursuit ethically legible even when it is removed from view.

changed_reading.before: Beyond that is only a neutral location outside a limit.
changed_reading.after: Beyond that can also expose an evasive strategy: relocating desire out of sight while still crossing the known limit.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The focus-only inventory for ابتغى contains a sexual-immorality branch, but the demonstrative ذلك remains unresolved without context.
baseline_models.mechanism: A sexualized branch of pursuit combines with the far side of an unnamed allowance and the explicit boundary-crosser label, yielding a live but not yet context-secured sexual reading.

activation_trace.role: Sexual immorality supplies a domain-specific candidate for what the pursuit could seek.
The far side supplies an exterior to a still-unresolved permitted domain.
Overstepping a bound turns the sexual candidate into a limit-violation model rather than a free association.

changed_reading.before: The focus alone leaves the object and domain of seeking unspecified.
changed_reading.after: The focus inventory raises sexual overreach as a specific candidate, while withholding certainty until the demonstrative is resolved.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: ابتغى and العادون can jointly carry images of spirited running and repeated pursuit across the far side named by وراء.
baseline_models.mechanism: The breach is kinetic rather than static: appetite gathers speed, crosses the perimeter, and continues in successive pursuit instead of stopping after one contact with the line.

activation_trace.role: A horse prancing with spirited pride gives the seeking motion self-exciting momentum.
The far side gives the accelerating motion a line to pass.
Running and hastening converts the transgressor label into an image of speed.
Successive pursuit makes the crossing repeat and continue rather than end at the first breach.

changed_reading.before: The transgressor has simply stepped once outside a rule.
changed_reading.after: The transgressor is also a pursuer whose appetite accelerates and keeps chasing beyond the stopping point.

context_deltas.mechanism: The far/near reversal makes وراء ذلك perspectival as well as spatial. Crossing can be enabled by treating the limit's consequence as remote, although the context reverses that estimate and presents it as near.

activation_trace.role: The heart's opinion and reflection makes their estimate of distance an interpretive judgment, not bare geometry.
Distance from nearness supplies the mistaken remote horizon.
Nearness reverses that horizon and collapses the imagined safety of distance.
The far side lets the focus inherit the context's contested depth perception.
Overstepping is the conduct that the false distance estimate helps enable.

structural_cues: The paired judgments in 70:6-7 explicitly reverse far and near before 70:31 uses the far-side term وراء.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opposed perceptions of distance and the focus's far-side construction; I infer that imagined remoteness can enable crossing, while a live alternative is that 70:6-7 concerns only the timing of the promised day.

changed_reading.before: The verse marks an objective perimeter and condemns crossing it.
changed_reading.after: It also diagnoses the depth-perception error by which a seeker treats the far side and its consequence as safely remote when it is near.

context_deltas.mechanism: The human disposition described before the exception list is asymmetrical: disturbance when harm arrives and a closed hand when good arrives. Seeking beyond a limit becomes one expression of the same acquisitive instability, taking outward while resisting outward obligation.

activation_trace.role: Anxious greed and quick agitation supplies the unstable appetite that the later disciplines answer.
Being struck by an effect makes the disposition reactive to what reaches it.
Withholding the hand from giving supplies the closed, possessive half of the appetite cycle.
Directed seeking is the outward reach through which the unstable appetite acts.
Overstepping into oppression marks the point where appetite becomes harm to another.

structural_cues: 70:19-21 states a general human disposition, and 70:22-35 forms an exception list that contains the focus.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies anxious greed, reactive contact, withholding, and then disciplined exceptions; I infer one appetite-control mechanism across the list, while the live alternative treats each listed virtue as independent.

changed_reading.before: The focus prohibits one isolated kind of excessive pursuit.
changed_reading.after: The focus becomes a diagnostic moment in an appetite cycle that reaches for more while withholding what should move toward others.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context distinguishes a legitimate request from overreach. A known, owned right is assigned to an asker and to one deprived; therefore seeking itself is not condemned. It becomes transgression when it proceeds beyond an established due.

activation_trace.role: A specific right belonging to its holder supplies the positive limit by which a request can be warranted.
Asking and requesting supplies a legitimate form of seeking immediately before the focus's pursuit language.
Deprivation and missing the sought object identifies a claimant whose lack does not cancel the assigned right.
Seeking is retained as a neutral motion whose legitimacy depends on the perimeter of right.
Overstepping into injustice distinguishes unwarranted acquisition from the context's rightful request.

structural_cues: 70:24-25 pairs a known right with the asker and deprived person shortly before 70:31 says whoever seeks beyond that.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a warranted claimant, a fixed right, and later pursuit beyond a limit; I infer a claim-versus-encroachment distinction, while the live alternative confines 70:24-25 to wealth without carrying its logic into 70:31.

changed_reading.before: Seeking is the suspicious act, and restraint means not asking for more.
changed_reading.after: Seeking is judged by entitlement: asking along a known right is protected, while pursuit beyond one's due becomes encroachment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate sequence resolves the focus's demonstrative. A vulnerable sexual opening is guarded; paired and held relations form stated exceptions; lack of blame marks their interior. Pursuit past that articulated perimeter is then named sexual transgression.

activation_trace.role: The bodily opening and genitals identifies the immediate sexual domain that the focus-only model could not resolve.
Preserving sanctity, covenant, and chastity makes the opening a guarded relational trust.
The marriage pair supplies one expressly admitted relation inside the perimeter.
Possession and authorized disposition supplies the second relation named inside the exception.
The right hand and right side fixes the bodily-legal expression attached to that second exception.
Blame for blameworthy conduct supplies the explicit negative whose absence marks the permitted interior.
Sexual immorality now becomes context-secured as the domain of pursuit rather than a focus-only possibility.
The far side locates the sought relation outside the two stated exceptions.
Overstepping a bound supplies the final classification of unlicensed sexual pursuit.

structural_cues: 70:29-31 is a continuous sequence of guarding, explicit exception, absence of blame, and pursuit beyond ذلك.
The demonstrative in 70:31 naturally resumes the bounded set just stated in 70:30.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the sexual opening, guard, two exceptions, no-blame interior, and the focus's demonstrative; I infer that ذلك resumes the whole permitted set, while a live alternative narrows it to the nearest exception alone.

changed_reading.before: Sexual overreach is only one branch-level candidate because the focus does not name its own domain.
changed_reading.after: The immediate context resolves the candidate into pursuit outside an explicitly guarded and excepted sexual perimeter.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus sits inside a maintenance system rather than a one-time ban. Continuous prayer precedes it, trusts and covenant follow it, and guarded prayer closes the list. Sexual restraint is therefore one practiced act of keeping entrusted limits over time.

activation_trace.role: Prayer as a binding practice supplies the repeated discipline at the list's opening side.
Continuance and stability turns that discipline into sustained maintenance.
Security and trust makes what follows the focus something held under confidence rather than available appetite.
A preserved covenant supplies an explicit relational boundary that must be kept.
Keeping and tending a covenant supplies the active stewardship opposed to acquisitive crossing.
Persistent maintenance closes the catalog with the same guarding logic used around the focus.
Seeking is the active pressure that the maintained trust-order must govern.
Overstepping names the failure of sustained guardianship and covenant keeping.

structural_cues: 70:23 and 70:34 bracket the virtue catalog with دوام الصلاة and حفظ الصلاة.
70:32 follows the focus immediately with trusts, covenant, and their active tending.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated prayer, guarding, trust, covenant, and tending around the focus; I infer one maintenance architecture in which sexual limits are entrusted, while the live alternative reads the items as adjacent but independent virtues.

changed_reading.before: The verse draws a sexual line that a person either crosses or does not cross in one act.
changed_reading.after: The verse tests a durable trust-practice: the line remains intact through repeated guarding, covenant keeping, and disciplined attention.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later scene repeats the focus's acquisitive trajectory at a larger scale. Those formed by the preceding disciplines are honored in gardens, while every outsider covets entry. Seeking beyond becomes an entitlement pattern: wanting admission to a protected good without the order that defines its interior.

activation_trace.role: Commendable honor marks the outcome assigned to the preceding disciplined group.
The heart's coveting and hope supplies the later analogue to seeking beyond.
Entering an interior supplies the desired crossing into a protected destination.
A garden enclosed and hidden by trees gives that desired interior a bounded image.
Pursuit connects the local boundary breach to the later coveting of entry.
The far side provides the exterior position from which admission is desired.
Boundary crossing distinguishes entitled entry from the honor granted to the disciplined group.

structural_cues: 70:35 assigns honored garden-interiority to the preceding group, then 70:38 questions each outsider's desire to enter it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies honored insiders followed by coveting and entry; I infer that the later admission scene scales up the focus's acquisitive crossing, while the live alternative treats it only as a separate resurrection claim.

changed_reading.before: Seeking beyond concerns only access to a prohibited relation.
changed_reading.after: It also models entitlement itself: trying to enter a protected good while bypassing the disciplines and relations that bound access.

context_deltas.mechanism: Plural risings and settings span the available horizon, and the following declaration denies that anyone can get beyond the replacing power described there. The focus's وراء therefore cannot promise a true outside; transgression is attempted flight within an enclosing jurisdiction.

activation_trace.role: Light rising from the east supplies one edge of the repeated cosmic horizon.
Sunset and the west supplies the opposite edge, completing the horizon's daily span.
One thing standing in another's place supplies the asserted power to replace the transgressing group.
Escaping or getting beyond a pursuer supplies the explicitly denied exit route.
The far side becomes an attempted outside that the context's full horizon refuses.
Running and hastening gives the attempted escape a kinetic form.

structural_cues: 70:40 names plural eastern and western points, and 70:41 immediately denies being outstripped.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the spanning horizons, replacement, and denied outstripping; I infer an enclosing jurisdiction that makes the focus's beyond illusory, while the live alternative reads 70:40-41 only as a claim of creative power.

changed_reading.before: Beyond that names a locally available exterior that the transgressor successfully reaches.
changed_reading.after: The seeker crosses a local allowance but never reaches an outside to accountability; every apparent beyond remains inside the total horizon.

context_deltas.mechanism: The legal noun العادون acquires a later kinetic echo. Self-directed, spirited pursuit beyond the limit is answered by rapid emergence and a compelled rush toward a visibly erected goal; the chosen direction of appetite becomes an imposed terminal trajectory.

activation_trace.role: Passing out to the exterior supplies the final scene's abrupt emergence into motion.
Speed as the opposite of slowness makes the emergence an explicit race-like movement.
An erected, conspicuous object supplies a visible terminal goal for the rush.
A stone erected for worship or slaughter keeps misdirected devotion alive as an alternative account of the goal.
An erected boundary or basin marker makes the goal also resemble the very kind of limit crossed in the focus.
The prancing, spirited run gives the original seeking a self-propelled kinetic image.
Running and hastening lets the transgressor label resonate directly with the final speed.
Successive pursuit links repeated appetite to the later unavoidable race toward one goal.

structural_cues: 70:43 explicitly combines emergence, speed, and motion toward an erected object.
The branchless و ف ض occurrence at 70:43 word 9 supports rushing only as a structural cue and is not used as a branch citation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies speed, emergence, an erected goal, and focus branches of spirited running; I infer a reversal from chosen pursuit to compelled trajectory, while the live alternative reads نصب as a cultic goal rather than a boundary marker.

changed_reading.before: العادون is solely a legal label for people who have crossed a limit.
changed_reading.after: The label also carries a kinetic warning: voluntary appetite rehearses the motion of a later, compelled race toward a fixed goal.

context_deltas.mechanism: Agency reverses at the close. The focus's person actively seeks and runs beyond; in the final scene the gaze is lowered, humiliation catches up, covers, and breaks the runner. The one who overran a limit becomes the one overrun.

activation_trace.role: Lowering and submission reverses the proud, outward orientation of the pursuing subject.
Overwhelming and covering transfers active force from the seeker to the humiliation that engulfs him.
Drawing near and catching up supplies the exact pursuit reversal: consequence overtakes the pursuer.
Being broken under compulsion supplies the terminal loss of the seeker's self-direction.
Intentional pursuit establishes the agency that the final scene reverses.
Running and hastening makes the later catching-up image mechanically visible.

structural_cues: 70:43-44 moves from rapid outward motion to lowered eyes and engulfing humiliation.
The demonstrative ذلك appears at the focus's boundary and again in 70:44's identification of the promised day.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies active pursuit, later catching-up, covering, and compelled abasement; I infer an agency reversal in which the crosser is crossed over, while the live alternative sees only ordinary sequence from sin to punishment.

changed_reading.before: The transgressor is the active party who successfully outruns the stated limit.
changed_reading.after: The apparent runner is temporally overtaken: the force projected beyond the limit returns as humiliation that catches, covers, and subdues.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it composes three medical branch images rather than the ordinary legal senses. It remains valid as a cross-domain model because every image is anchored to a focus word and all three describe propagation past an original site. Downstream prose should render it only as a contained material analogy for how a breach spreads, never as a lexical translation of the ayah.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ابتغى, وراء, and العادون each offer a branch in which corruption moves beyond its starting site.

activation_trace.role: A wound swelling and spreading into corruption supplies the initiating lesion-like breach.
An illness eating into the belly or lung carries the breach behind the surface into an interior.
Contagion and transmission completes the model by moving damage from one site to another.

changed_reading.before: A transgression is a discrete crossing completed at the boundary.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, a breach can behave like an infection: it passes the surface, enters an interior, and propagates beyond the initiating act.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant split mappings from ع د و to counting and return/habit. It remains anchored to العادون and is useful for exposing accumulation and repetition already compatible with the dominant boundary sense. Downstream prose must label it a mapping-level activation, not offer counted or habitual as the word's direct gloss here.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The packet maps العادون not only to dominant boundary-crossing branches but also to non-dominant counting and habituation inventories.

activation_trace.role: The dominant image of crossing a bound keeps the outlier attached to the ordinary transgressor classification.
Enumerating what is counted makes separate crossings accumulate into an inspectable tally.
Habit, practiced familiarity, and repetition makes repeated crossing settle into a disposition.

changed_reading.before: One forbidden crossing is enough to produce a static legal label.
changed_reading.after: As a contained split-root activation, crossings can also be imagined as counted repetitions that train the seeker into a settled habit.

strongest_changes: The immediate context resolves the focus-only sexual candidate into a guarded exception perimeter whose exterior is explicitly transgressive.
The known right of the asker distinguishes warranted seeking from acquisitive encroachment, so seeking is judged by entitlement rather than condemned in itself.
The closing rush and humiliation reverse agency: the one who runs beyond a limit is finally caught, covered, and subdued.
The east-west horizon and denial of outstripping make every apparent beyond local; there is no exterior to accountability.
summary.what_was_special: The packet activated one mechanism across legal, spatial, temporal, and kinetic registers without collapsing them: a defined allowance, disciplined maintenance of that allowance, distorted desire for its exterior, and a final reversal in which the pursuer is overtaken.
remaining_uncertainties: The exact grammatical reach of ذلك can resume the whole permitted set in 70:30 or be read more narrowly toward its nearest member.
The catalog-wide appetite and trust models depend on reading adjacent virtues as one maintenance system rather than as independent traits.
The erected object in 70:43 remains live as either a conspicuous goal, a boundary-like marker, or a cultic stone, so the kinetic model should preserve that plurality.
The medical and counted-habit models are branch-valid but form-distant and must remain exploratory rather than lexical glosses.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Transgression is movement beyond an articulated boundary.** *Al-ʿādūn* activates **ع د و, B001, “overstepping a bound into injustice,”** while *warāʾa dhālika* supplies the spatial structure and *ibtaghā* supplies directed seeking. I infer that desire becomes injustice when it treats a stated relational limit as terrain to cross. The ayah reads as a movement model of wrongdoing, not a free-floating label.

2. **Haste is latent inside boundary-crossing.** **ع د و, B002, “running and hastening,”** is activated by the surah’s recurrent rushing: anxious *halūʿ*, the forward-hurrying crowd (70:36), and the grave-exiters racing in 70:43. I infer that unregulated desire compresses deliberation into rapid crossing. This reading connects sexual transgression to the surah’s larger pathology of urgency.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The forward-hurrying crowd in 70:36 and the grave-exiters in 70:43 activated **ع د و B002** behind legal transgression. Later motion imagery made overstepping feel temporally hurried as well as spatially beyond bounds.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Truthful performance versus fabricated interior
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Speech is tested against action and inward condition; invention and concealed corruption fail that test.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: truthful utterance `quranic:root_000852:B001/m01`; complete, sound condition `quranic:root_000852:B003/m01`; promise realized in action `quranic:root_000852:B004/m01`; fabricated discourse `quranic:root_000434:B007/m01`; hidden interior `quranic:root_000464:B003/m01`; concealed corruption `quranic:root_000464:B004/m01`; receiving and learning words `quranic:root_001372:B011/m01`; rhetorical concealment behind another meaning `quranic:root_001642:B005/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Truth is correspondence carried into performance. Fabrication, hidden interior, and rhetorical cover separate surface utterance from inward state, while testimony reunites what is said, known, and done.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Desire for an interior can be manipulated by a visible lure, converting self-directed approach into capture.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Garden entry becomes a hunting scene with decoy bird, set snare, raised marker, game, and protective screen.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Screen and shield cannot create belonging
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A would-be entrant equips himself with cover, shield, or tent, but these defenses only hide and do not authorize entry.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: protective shield `quranic:root_000266:B008/m01`; armor `quranic:root_000121:B005/m01`; mosquito-screen tent `quranic:root_001315:B006/m01`; material covering `quranic:root_001307:B001/m01`; rhetorical concealment `quranic:root_001642:B005/m01`; concealed sword under a garment `quranic:root_000819:B005/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Cover and shield can prevent contact or detection, but they cannot establish a rightful place inside. The concealed weapon even makes defensive appearance compatible with hostile intent, sharpening the difference between protected residence and disguised intrusion.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 70:19-44] Race, Wager, and the False Prize
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Competitive precedence promises a prize to the swift, but sovereign pursuit removes the contestants' control over both course and award.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The scene includes first and second horses, stake, military pay, gambling arrows, divided lots, reward-seeking gift, and losing throw.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Ordered race and ranked finish
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Horses compete for precedence, a second runner follows the leader, and body mechanics determine rank.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: racing into first place `quranic:root_000671:B001/m01`; stake placed for the winner `quranic:root_000671:B002/m01`; second horse following the leader's flank `quranic:root_000879:B006/m01`; horse whose rear feet match the forefeet `quranic:root_000347:B014/m01`; horse prancing in its run `quranic:root_000138:B007/m01`; market activity rising `quranic:root_001273:B018/m01`; walking lightly on foot `quranic:root_001525:B012/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The race has a precise order: leader, close second, stake, and gait. That intelligible sport frame is then broken by `70:41`, where no created runner can establish the decisive lead required to escape replacement.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 70:19-44] Textile Cover, Hidden Interior, and Chromatic Exposure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A surface may shelter or disguise an interior, but wear, opening, and color eventually disclose what the cover carried.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Night-cover, wrap, mosquito tent, worn cloth, concealed sword, inner corruption, dyed sign, black raven, and whitening hair form a disclosure process.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Concealed interior and disguised breach
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A protected inside stores heart, weapon, secret, or corruption, and may present a misleading outer face.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: hidden heart and inward matter `quranic:root_000266:B010/m01`; rhetorical cover that displays other than intended `quranic:root_001642:B005/m01`; private interior `quranic:root_000464:B003/m01`; concealed corruption `quranic:root_000464:B004/m01`; interlocking internal parts `quranic:root_000464:B008/m01`; denial covering truth `quranic:root_001307:B003/m01`; confused intermixture `quranic:root_001423:B009/m01`; concealed sword or calamity `quranic:root_000819:B005/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Interior is morally neutral until its contents are known: heart, interlocked structure, weapon, and corruption can all sit behind a cover. Disguise occurs when the outer surface asserts protection while the inner assembly carries breach.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 70:19-44] Food, Fire, and the Throat of Processing
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Material is transformed by heat, drying, chewing, swallowing, and digestion into nourishment, residue, or injury.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Sun-curing, spark, roasting drippings, kindled fire, stirred drink, saliva, choking, esophagus, feast, and intensified grinding form one alimentary mechanism.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Drying, kindling, and rendered drippings
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Food is exposed to sun, cut, heated, and stirred until moisture leaves and fat or blood flows.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: sun-curing meat `quranic:root_000790:B002/m01`; laying food in sun to dry `quranic:root_000787:B002/m01`; flying sparks `quranic:root_000787:B003/m01`; fat dripping from roast meat `quranic:root_000787:B005/m01`; enduring fire and heat `quranic:root_000879:B001/m01`; hidden fire struck from flint `quranic:root_001642:B002/m01`; stirring drink or blood `quranic:root_000446:B003/m01`; cutting meat and incising a wound `quranic:root_001638:B002/m01`; calming a boiling pot with water `quranic:root_000501:B002/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Processing alternates removal and addition: sun removes moisture, cutting opens matter, fire renders fat, stirring mixes fluid, and water quiets boil. The chain clarifies how the same heat can prepare provision or materialize punishment depending on its end.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A breached body can swell, suppurate, transmit harm, and lose the alignment needed for free movement.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Incision, boil, lung disease, facial palsy, spreading wound, transmitted illness, chest frame, long neck, eye swelling, and overloaded limbs form a clinical scene.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Incision, swelling, and suppuration
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Tissue is cut, a wound spreads, pus consumes the interior, and a swelling emerges visibly.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: festering wound `quranic:root_000138:B004/m01`; boil or bodily eruption `quranic:root_000400:B004/m01`; cutting and shredding `quranic:root_000787:B004/m01`; incision in flesh or wound `quranic:root_001638:B002/m01`; lung or internal suppuration `quranic:root_001642:B001/m01`; severe bodily disease `quranic:root_001077:B017/m01`; facial palsy and distortion `quranic:root_001372:B001/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The wound develops causally: incision opens, tissue swells, corruption travels inward, a boil pushes outward, and distortion appears in the face. Hidden pathology becomes visible form.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Contact and transmitted affliction
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Harm reaches by touch, spreads from one body to another, and imposes a burden beyond ordinary capacity.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: madness-like affliction by touch `quranic:root_001423:B003/m01`; adverse impact `quranic:root_001423:B004/m01`; disease crossing between bodies `quranic:root_000993:B006/m01`; concealed internal defect `quranic:root_000464:B004/m01`; bodily disease `quranic:root_001077:B017/m01`; forced burden beyond capacity `quranic:root_000606:B003/m01`; corrupt wound spreading past its boundary `quranic:root_000138:B004/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Contact is the path by which a local defect becomes relational harm. Touch, transmission, internal concealment, and boundary-crossing explain why guarding is preventative care, while imposed burden describes the endpoint when the body can no longer contain the process.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 70:19-44] Concealed Fetus, Birth, and Known Material Origin
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Creation proceeds from hidden material through gestation, parturition, reception, and social incorporation.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Fetus, sealed passage, intercourse, afterbirth, midwife, rapid conception, nursing household, partial breeding, and marriage payment form one life-cycle.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Marriage as incorporation into a household
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Sexual pairing is recognized through contract, dower, and the rearing of children across household lines.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: marital spouse `quranic:root_000652:B002/m01`; joining partners `quranic:root_000652:B003/m01`; marriage contract `quranic:root_001444:B004/m01`; marriage payment `quranic:root_000852:B007/m01`; dependent stepchild `quranic:root_000532:B005/m01`; sexual misconduct outside the bond `quranic:root_000138:B005/m01`; entry into marital intimacy `quranic:root_000464:B002/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Marriage is social incorporation rather than contact alone. Pairing, contract, dower, intimacy, and care for a child from an earlier union build the household boundary that transgression bypasses.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi veya ihtiyacı isteme ve arama çekirdeğini açıkça verir; ayrıca bir başkası için arama, onun arayışına yardım etme ve bazı kullanımlarda arayışı yoğunlaştırma yönlerini de destekler. Bu nedenle sunulan dal kimliği kaynak kapsamını doğru temsil eder.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, doğrudan arama ve isteme alanındadır; haksızlık, yara bozulması, cinsel davranış, yağış, at koşusu ve askerî öncülük anlamlarını içermez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın dalı kapsar; başka dallara veya yalnızca belirli söz öbeklerine bağlı anlamlar bu genel arama anlamına aktarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi, ihtiyacı veya amacı istemek, aramak ve ona yönelmek; kimi kullanımda bunu özel bir çabayla ya da ölçüyü aşan bir istekle yapmaktır. Eylem, bir başkası için aramayı veya onun arayışına yardım ederek onu arayan duruma getirmeyi de kapsayabilir.

facets.statement: Bir şeyi, ihtiyacı veya amacı istemek, aramak ve ona yönelmek.
Arayış, kimi kullanımda özel çaba göstermeyi veya ölçüyü aşacak kadar yoğun istemeyi bildirir.
Bir başkası için bir şeyi aramak ya da o kişinin arayışına yardım ederek onu arayan duruma getirmek.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, dalın temelini bir şeyi isteme ve arama olarak ortaklaşa verir. Aynı toplu kanıt, aranan ihtiyacı veya amacı, çabalı arayışı ve bir başkasının aramasına yardım etme yönünü de kapsar.

concept_gloss.text: bir şeyi arayıp istemek; başkası için aramak veya arayışına yardım etmek
concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın doğrudan arama çekirdeğini ve katılımcının bir başkası yararına aradığı ya da ona yardım ettiği genişlemeyi birlikte karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Aranan şeyi, isteme ve arama eylemini, başkası yararına aramayı ve arayışa yardım etmeyi korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı belirli bir sözlük biriminin uygun düşme, yapılabilir veya kolaylaştırılabilir olma ve bağlama göre hak edilmiş sayılma anlamlarıyla sınırlar. Sunulan kimlik, doğrudan isteme eylemi değil, eylemin kişiye veya koşullara uygunluğu ve imkânı olarak kaynakla uyumludur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, uygunluk, elverişlilik ve hak edilmişlik bildiren özel bir birimdir; yalın kökün genel arama ya da haksızlık anlamı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnızca kanıtlanan özel sözlük birimine bağlıdır; uygunluk ve yapılabilirlik anlamları yalın kökün genel anlamı gibi sunulmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir eylemin kişiye veya duruma uygun düşmesi; bağlama göre yapılabilir, kolaylaştırılabilir ya da hak edilmiş olmasıdır. Olumsuz biçimi, eylemin uygun veya mümkün olmadığını bildirir.

facets.statement: Bir eylemin kişiye veya duruma uygun düşmesi ve yapılmasının yerinde olması.
Bağlama göre eylemin kolaylaşması, mümkün olması veya kişinin ona hak kazanmış sayılması.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt, özel bir sözlük biriminin eyleme uygunluk bildirdiğinde birleşir. Kaynak ifadesi bu uygunluğu yapılabilirlik, kolaylaşma ve hak edilmişlik yönleriyle açıklar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi dalı sınırı aşma, haksızlık etme, bir başkasına karşı üstünlük taslama ve doğru olandan yanlış olana yönelme ekseninde kurar. Karşılıklı haksızlık ve kibirlenme de aynı sınır aşımı çekirdeğine bağlıdır; sunulan dal kimliği bu yapıyı doğru yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dalın çekirdeği haksız ve saldırgan sınır aşımıdır; genel arama, yara bozulması ve öteki özel dallar yalnızca aynı biçimi taşımaları nedeniyle buraya katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın haksız sınır aşımını; birine karşı yöneltilen, fail adıyla belirtilen ve karşılıklı gerçekleşen özel kullanımlardan açıkça ayırır.

concept_map.definition: Hak veya ölçü sınırını aşarak haksızlık etmek, başkasına karşı saldırgan biçimde üstünlük taslamak ya da doğru olandan yanlış olana yönelmektir. Eylem tek yönlü olabileceği gibi tarafların birbirine haksızlık etmesi biçiminde de gerçekleşebilir.

facets.statement: Hak veya ölçü sınırını aşarak haksızlık ve baskı uygulamak.
Bir başkasına karşı üstünlük taslayıp saldırgan biçimde haddini aşmak.
Tarafların karşılıklı olarak birbirine haksızlık etmesi ve sınırı aşması.
Sınır aşımını doğru olandan yanlış olana yönelme veya kibirlenme olarak açıklamak.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, haksızlık ve ölçüyü aşma çekirdeğinde birleşir. Toplu ifade bu çekirdeği başkasına karşı üstünlük kurma, karşılıklı haksızlık, kibir ve doğru olandan sapma yönleriyle genişletir.

concept_gloss.text: haddi aşarak haksızlık etmek

concept_gloss.text: atın koşarken çalımlı ve neşeli davranması
concept_gloss.applicability: Atın koşu biçimindeki hızdan çok tavrı, kendini gösterişi ve neşeyi belirten söz öbeği için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Atı, koşu bağlamını, çalımlı kendini gösterişi ve neşeli tavrı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Atın koşu sırasında yalnızca hızlanmadığını, hareketleriyle canlılık ve gösteriş sergilediğini anlatan bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Koşan atı, çalımlı gösterişi ve neşeli canlılığı korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: atın koşarken çalımlı ve neşeli davranması

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal koşan atın çalımlı, kendini gösteren ve neşeli tavrını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal koşunun şiddetini, alevlenir gibi hızlanmasını ve toz kaldırmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da atın güçlü bir koşu içindeki görünüşünü betimler.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal tavır ve neşe, komşu dal ise hızın fiziksel şiddeti ve toz sonucu üzerindedir; aynı sahaya ait olsalar da çekirdekleri farklıdır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal atın koşarken gösterdiği çalım ve neşeyi temel alır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal hayvanın canlılık ve hızla ön ayaklarına yüklenerek koşma biçimini temel alır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her ikisi de canlı ve hareketli bir koşu sırasında hayvanın görünür davranışını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal duygusal ve gösterişli tavrı, komşu dal bedensel yüklenme biçimini anlatır; bu yüzden yalnızca aynı alandadırlar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal koşu boyunca süren çalımlı ve neşeli tavrı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal atın yarışta bir hamlede ileri atılması ve öteki atların önüne çıkmasını bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da koşan atın dikkat çeken hareketini betimler.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal bir tavır niteliğidir; komşu dal ise tek bir itiliş ve yarış içindeki ilerleme hareketidir. Süreç ve sonuç bakımından ayrılırlar.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; seçilen üç karşılaştırma tavır ve neşeyi, koşu şiddeti, bedensel yüklenme ve yarış hamlesinden ayırır.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه بغي الفرس في عدوه، أي اختياله ومرحه
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يقال فرس باغ كما نبه الخليل، وليس هذا ظلم الإنسان ولا طلب الشيء
branches.source_phrase_ar: اختيال الفرس ومرحه بغي؛ لا يقال فرس باغ (maqayis)؛ البغي في عدو الفرس اختيال ومرح؛ لا يقال فرس باغ (ayn)؛ البغي اختيال ومرح في الفرس؛ لا يقال فرس باغ (sihah)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi çoğul biçimi ordunun gelişinden önce giden öncüler, tekil biçimi de bu topluluğun bir üyesi olarak tanımlar. Sunulan kimlik bu askerî öncülük anlamını, aynı biçimin kadınlara ilişkin öteki dalından açıkça ayırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal ordudan önce ilerleyen öncü kişi veya topluluğa özgüdür; aynı biçimli kadın adlarıyla ve genel ilerleme ya da yol kesme anlamlarıyla karıştırılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım kanıtlanan yalın tekil ve çoğul adları kapsar; komşu kartlardaki keşif, casusluk veya sınır nöbeti görevleri zorunlu özellik olarak eklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Ordunun gelişinden önce ilerleyen öncü kişiler veya öncü topluluktur; tekil biçim bu öncülerden bir kişiyi belirtir.

facets.statement: Ordunun gelişinden önce ilerleyen öncü kişiler veya öncü topluluk.
Öncü topluluğun tek bir üyesini belirten tekil ad.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar çoğul adın ordudan önce ilerleyen öncüleri belirttiği konusunda birleşir. Toplu kanıt, tekil adın da bu öncülerden bir kişiyi gösterdiğini bildirir.

concept_gloss.text: ordudan önce ilerleyen öncüler
concept_gloss.applicability: Öncü topluluğun orduya göre zaman ve konum bakımından önde bulunmasını doğal ve kısa biçimde karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Öncü kişileri, ordudan önce ilerlemeyi ve topluluk anlamını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir topluluğun ordudan önce ilerlediği askerî bağlamlarda doğal çoğul veya topluluk karşılığıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Askerî topluluğu ve ana ordudan önce ilerleme ilişkisini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Tekil biçimin öncü topluluktaki bir kişiyi belirttiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Tek bir kişiyi ve onun öncü topluluğa üyeliğini korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dalın kanıtlanan sınırı ordudan önce ilerlemektir; düşmanı gözetleme zorunlu değildir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, düşmanın durumunu görmek üzere özellikle gönderilen keşif öncüsünü gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da ordunun önünde görev yapan askerî öncü kişi veya topluluğu anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Öncülük çekirdeğinde yaklaşırlar; ancak komşu dalın düşmanı gözetleme amacı, odak dalın kaynakça zorunlu kılınmayan özel bir görev sınırıdır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal ana ordudan önce giden belirli bir öncü topluluğu adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal genel olarak bir topluluğun en önde ve en hızlı giden ilk kişilerini, asker dışındaki gruplarda da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da bir topluluktan önce ilerleyen kişileri anlatabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal askerî öncü topluluğa bağlıdır; komşu dal ise hız ve ilk sırada bulunmayı daha geniş insan gruplarına yayar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal ordudan önce ilerleyen öncüleri temel alır ve kalıcı bir mevzi gerektirmez.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal silahlı gözcüleri, sınır veya gözetleme mevzilerini ve haber toplama görevini birlikte kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal ordunun güvenliği için önde bulunan silahlı kişiler alanında kesişebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın kurucu özelliği ordudan önce ilerlemektir; komşu dalda ise mevzi, silah ve gözetleme görevi çekirdeği belirler.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adayların tamamı değerlendirildi; seçilen üç ilişki genel askerî öncüyü keşif görevlisi, hızlı önden giden kişi ve sınır gözcüsünden ayırır.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه البغايا بمعنى الطلائع التي تكون قبل ورود الجيش، والواحدة بغية
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس بغايا بمعنى الجواري أو الإماء أو الفاجرات
branches.source_phrase_ar: البغايا الطلائع الواحدة بغية أيضا (ayn)؛ البغايا أيضا الطلائع التي تكون قبل ورود الجيش (sihah)

root_profile.summary: Bu kökün dalları bir şeyi arayıp istemeyi; uygun veya yapılabilir olmayı; haksızca sınır aşmayı; yaranın bozulmasını; evlilik dışı cinsel davranışı; aşırı yağışı; koşan atın çalımlı tavrını ve ordudan önce ilerleyen öncüleri anlatır. Anlamlar, ortak biçim çevresinde belirgin biçimde ayrılmış sekiz sözlüksel alan oluşturur.
